title: Siena no. 17: Bartolomeo Tantucci in the cipher of the Balia, 25 August 1528

documents.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Siena, Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 17; DECODE R4805 (Concistoro_2308_59)
documents.route: Bartolomeo Tantucci -> messer Antonio del Vescovo, rector of the cathedral, member of the Balia

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the sheet; clear frame and connecting words only.

transcription.notes: 282 cipher signs in 8 lines (CTTS lines 5-12 of P1). Count from the report, not re-measured. George Lasry names accurate transcription as the main obstacle in this fascicle. The project's own 24 Sept transcription is kept in project_attempt/ and was not used for the reading.

system.summary: Homophonic letter substitution without word division, up to five signs per vowel, doubled letters with two different signs, and the 'che' abbreviation as a sign.
system.doubled_letters: Every double letter written with two different signs.
system.sibling_key: The docket calls it 'quella di Balia'; no filed key in fasc. 1 was matched. Compared sign by sign with nos. 15 and 5 (report key figures): a different key.
system.notes: Key figure in key_lasry.jpg (report p. 25). Four signs listed as unknown.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment on DECODE or in print known; the project's 24 Sept survey left it unread.

conditions.human_role: George Lasry transcribed in CTTS and ran the solution with Claude; this project filed his report (no re-reading).
models: Claude (version not stated in the report)

solution.what: Project survey (siena1421): transcription of no. 17 (agent A) and homophonic annealing; filed keys R4760, R4768, R4778 compared. Not read; closed as too short.
George Lasry transcribed the 282 cipher signs in CTTS.
Key recovered by Claude (frequency and contact analysis, isomorphs, cribs), per the report.
About 85% read; the opening words of two points and one phrase remain uncertain.

This project compared the report's key figures for nos. 17, 15 and 5 sign by sign: shared shapes take different values (the square-U sign is i in no. 17, n in no. 15, o in no. 5). Three keys, three entries.

No. 17: George Lasry's key table (signs cut from the manuscript) matched by shape and count to the sign names of the project's own 24 Sept transcription (project_attempt/no17.txt, agent A, made before his work); our 283 tokens deciphered with his key, without fitting, and aligned with his reading: 252 agree (89.0%) with the first identification, 263 (92.9%) after re-identifying three signs by count (our 7 = his open A, SS = his P '+δ', 5o = his T); the rest fall on his own uncertain words ('el Mustetto', 'Otto', 'lco[..]stren') and on our 6, which merges his O and V. research/siena2308/verify_lasry.py no17.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): George Lasry's decipherment and translation (reading.txt, translation.txt, lasry_report.md), his key figure and table; transcription = this project's 24 Sept one (project_attempt/no17.txt), his CTTS transcription not being in the repository.

validation.notes: contributed reading: George Lasry's sign-level CTTS transcription and key are not in the repository, so no token alignment can be scored

outcome.method_basis: The report says the key was recovered by Claude from frequency and contact analysis, isomorphs and cribs; no decipherment or filed key was used.

gaps.item: opening words of the second and third points and one phrase ('lco[??]stren[?]niare'), about 15% of the 282 signs
gaps.detail: Uncertain in George Lasry's own reading; workable from his CTTS transcription and the image, not yet retried.

gaps.item: 'el Mustetto', the Cardinal of Naples, the Countess, the 'Otto', the writer's place
gaps.detail: Historical identifications open in the report.

credits.note: Transcription in CTTS and key recovered ciphertext-only with Claude; reading and translation (report pp. 25-27).
credits.source: Email and report to Daniel Bourdeau, 17 Oct 2026

texts.label: No. 17 (R4805), Bartolomeo Tantucci to Antonio del Vescovo, Sarteano(?), 25 August 1528 (George Lasry)
texts.summary: Bartolomeo Tantucci to messer Antonio del Vescovo, rector of the cathedral, in the cipher of the Balìa, 25 (or 20) August 1528: bishoprics promised to 'the nephews' by 'el Mustetto'(?), the Cardinal of Naples (Vincenzo Carafa?) and Pitigliano, and the 'Otto'(?) wanting to constrain Pitigliano; 'Parlo breve et in substantia perché la cifra vuol così.' Decryption and translation are George Lasry's; the transcription linked is this project's independent one of 24 Sept 2026, on which his key was checked (92.9% agreement), since his CTTS transcription is not in the repository.
